current.text: He played only three games for Utah last season, so this is his first full season with the Jazz.
He is expected to start at power forward next to Jusuf Nurkic and to close games at center.
Jaxson Hayes started at center in the preseason because Utah does not want Jackson playing much center.
He should play more minutes in Utah. His usage will likely drop because he shares the ball with Lauri Markkanen, Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson.
With Walker Kessler gone, his blocks may rise. Josh thinks 2 blocks per game is possible with less offensive usage, but not a return to 3.
The experts disagree on his rebounds. Leaf projects a double-double and his easiest baskets in years from slipping screens, while Josh says 10 rebounds per game would be a huge outcome.
He is expected to be better than last season, but not to reach his Memphis career highs.

Experts call his market price too low. They see a Yahoo ADP around 55 as good value and an ESPN rank of 82 as too low. One expert ranks him 36th in category leagues and calls him a target there about two rounds after that rank.
In a 9-cat mock draft he went in round 4 to a team building toward blocks with poor assists.
Utah is expected to be a good team that tries to win, with about 43 wins and a playoff spot. Experts call fears of tanking and shutdowns misplaced.
Josh expects minutes and usage on the Jazz to be all over the place early in the season.

durable.text: He is one of very few bigs who can block about two shots and score about 20 points per game. His blocks are far above the top 250 pool.
He is a poor rebounder for a big man.
He is usually worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He has not been able to play center over the last 4 to 5 years. He plays best next to a big, physical center.
His turnovers are high for a forward or center.

note: The market prices him low, with average costs of 14.6 USD on Yahoo and 7.3 USD on ESPN. That is well below his 25 USD Yahoo value and the 29 USD our league paid last season. The experts rank him about 36th in category formats, so he is a good buy anywhere near his average cost. He fits blocks builds and punt TO builds, and he can help punt AST teams. Early in the season, check three things: whether his minutes go above 30, whether his blocks get back toward 2 per game with Kessler gone, and how much usage he keeps next to Markkanen, George and Peterson.
